sentences.text:
Rahul Gupta vs State Of U.P. And Another on 11 December,
2024
High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
?Neutral Citation No. - 2024:Ahc:194168
Court No. - 79
Case :- Application U/S 482 No. - 36876 of 2024
Applicant :- Rahul Gupta
Opposite Party :- State of U.P. and Another
Counsel for Applicant :- Srijan Pandey
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Arun Kumar Singh Deshwal,J.

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 1. Heard learned counsel for the applicant and Sri P. P. Tiwari, learned A.G.A. for the State.

2.  The present 482 Cr.P.C. application has been filed to quash the summoning order dated 01.04.2008 as well as entire proceeding of Case No.1918 of 2008 (State vs. Rahul Gupta), under Sections 7, 16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 (hereinafter referred to 'Food Adulteration Act') pending before the Court of Ld. Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Court No.2,
Allahabad.
3.

entities.text: Case No.1918 of 2008 (State vs. Rahul Gupta)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text:
Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Court No.2,
Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Contention of the learned counsel for the applicant is that the Food Analyst report was received on 10.11.2006, but complaint was filed in October, 2008, therefore, complaint is barred by latches.
4.

The second submission of learned counsel for the applicant is that after taking the sample, the same should have been produced before the Magistrate under Section 11 (4) of the Food and Rahul Gupta vs State Of U.P. And Another on 11 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/192971294/
1 Adulteration Act but the same was not produced before the Magistrate, therefore, entire prosecution is bad in law.

entities.text: Rahul Gupta vs State Of U.P. And Another on 11 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 5. Per contra, learned A.G.A. submits that the impugned complaint was filed in the year 2008 and the applicant has also appeared before the Court and the matter was posted for proceeding under Section 244 Cr.P.C., thereafter, the matter kept on adjourning and finally after almost 16 years, the applicant cannot approach this Court to quash the impugned proceeding on the ground raised by the applicant.
Therefore, there is no illegality in the impugned proceeding.

6. Considering the rival submissions of learned counsel for the parties and on perusal of the record,
it appears that the impugned complaint was filed in the year 2008 after taking permission from the required authority, therefore, at this stage it cannot be said that the complaint was time barred.

7. So far as the second contention that the sample was not produced within a period of seven days before Magistrate concerned as required by Section 11 (4) is concerned, that ground is available to the applicant at the time of trial, however, this ground cannot be considered at this stage to quash the impugned proceeding which is after 16 years of the filing the complaint.

8. Therefore, this Court does not find any illegality in the impugned proceeding, however,
considering the fact that impugned complaint has been pending since 2008 at the stage of 244 Cr.P.C for the reason, prosecution witness could not appear and it is also clear from the order sheet that the present applicant has also remained absent for a long time, therefore, the Court below is directed to conclude the trial of complaint case No.1918/2008 (State Vs. Rahul Gupta) under Section 7, 16 of the Food and Adulteration Act pending in the Court of Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Court No.2, Allahabad expeditiously, without granting any unnecessary adjournment to any of the parties.

entities.text: Court of Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Court No.2, Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
9. From the perusal of the record, it also appears that after the issuance of summons, 'non-bailable warrant' against the applicant has been issued without recording any reason which is against the provisions of Section 87 Cr.P.C., therefore, non-bailable warrant issued against the applicant is hereby quashed and the applicant will appear before the court below on the next date failing which court below will proceed against the applicant in accordance with law.
10. Registrar (Compliance) is directed to send a copy of this order to the concerned Magistrate for necessary compliance.

11. Registrar (Compliance) is also directed to send a copy of this order to the Commissioner, Food and Civil Supply who will look into the issue and ensure that his department will properly pursue the complaint case No.1918 of 2008 pending in the Court of ACJM, Court No.2, Allahabad.

entities.text: Court of ACJM, Court No.2, Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 12. With the aforesaid observations, the application is disposed of.
